evidence.snippet:
## What survives: conflicting reports

The grain is the claim. Each lens sighting is one claim, and a lowering belongs to the stored record for its claim.

- The strongest verdict still wins: `confirmed` over `plausible` over `refuted`, as [conflicting verifier reports](2026-10-06-verifier-conflicting-reports.md) set it. A weaker report leaves the record unchanged.
- On equal verdicts for one claim, the record keeps the higher severity. A later equal report never weakens a stored one. So two `confirmed` reports that disagree on a lowering leave the finding unlowered, in either order.
- When an equal report replaces a stored one, the record keeps the winning report's reason and evidence.
- The merged defect takes the highest severity among its claims after lowering. A claim no verifier judged keeps its own severity.

The verifier has one chance per claim, by design, so that a second call can never be used to lower: a report whose lowering the fence refused is stored unlowered, and a later equal report does not correct it. So that the one chance is a fair one, the label line Melian writes for each claim, outside the boundary, names the severity the lens reported.

verification.reason: The base decision 2026-10-13-re-scope-held-for-the-compiler is ACTIVE at base. It says: "On equal verdicts for one claim, the record keeps the higher severity. A later equal report never weakens a stored one. So two `confirmed` reports that disagree on a lowering leave the finding unlowered, in either order." Base code implemented this in `after`/`#stronger`. At head, `whole()` is false for an equal-verdict report with different JSON. `refusal()` then throws unless the report adds a new `different` answer. `after()` keeps the stored, lowered report. So a lowered `confirmed` followed by an unlowered `confirmed` leaves the claim lowered, where base left it unlowered and blocking. The new head decision (2026-11-28) is not an active base decision, so it cannot excuse the departure. Its own "What this gives up" section admits the change: "a confirmed lowering cannot be withdrawn... Under the old rule that later report won, and the claim went back up." The base reason still holds. A lowering is a weakening of the blocking set, so the safe side on conflicting equal reports is the higher severity. The head makes the first lowering sticky and takes away the fail-closed outcome.

Letting `different` win keeps [the dismissal decision](2026-11-08-dismissal-carries-to-restatement.md)'s fail-closed path, where a `different` answer leaves the finding live. evidence.snippet: A verifier that wants to correct its own reason at the same verdict cannot. It can only send a stronger verdict. Nothing is stronger than confirmed, so a confirmed lowering cannot be withdrawn by the verifier: a later confirmed report that holds the claim at the lens's severity is refused, and the claim stays one step down. Under the old rule that later report won, and the claim went back up. The maintainer accepted this cost on 2026-11-28, in the coordinator's session ("A, and read"), since the lowering still needs evidence at the head and passes the fence. A refused report is an error the verifier reads, and a verifier that never sends an accepted report leaves its claim unjudged, so the review reads not reviewed, as it does today for any claim the verifier skips.
